original_test_intent: Read one validated Manager NetworkProtocol resource and inventory configured management services and ports without changing service or network state.
original_method: Resolve the Manager's advertised NetworkProtocol URI, issue one trusted GET, validate resource identity and protocol/service schema, redact endpoints and compare optional project expectations without remediation.

safety_requirements: Never PATCH, POST, restart or reset services

agent_execution_scope: Bind BMC, Manager and firmware identity

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The GET fits service metadata retrieval, but `-k`, hardcoded credentials, log clearing, unredacted full output and readability-only acceptance are unsafe and insufficient.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use the Manager's canonical NetworkProtocol link for one trusted GET, validate the complete service/protocol schema, redact endpoints and report any policy mismatch without changing settings.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The Manager NetworkProtocol GET and 15/10 timing remain; no ManagerId, enabled service, port or desired setting is inferred.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Produce a typed protocol/service matrix from the canonical resource and separate observation from any later approved configuration change.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds identity/schema validation, endpoint privacy, policy comparison and an explicit no-remediation boundary while preserving logs.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Covers reported NetworkProtocol configuration only; it does not probe service connectivity, authentication, certificate validity or PATCH behavior.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: An enabled flag does not prove reachability, and a configured port can be filtered or occupied; active connectivity requires a separately scoped test.

project_override_considerations: Project expected services and ports are comparisons only. A mismatch must be reported for engineer judgment and cannot trigger automatic enable/disable or port changes.
expected_evidence: HTTP status/content type/timing and restricted raw hash
Proof no PATCH/POST/restart/reset/network change or log clear occurred

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The title, path and GET consistently describe reading Manager NetworkProtocol. Unsafe setup and weak criteria are deficiencies, not competing semantics.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Normal identity, access, schema and redaction inputs suffice for deterministic read-only automation.

review_improvement: Changes a raw service-configuration dump into a typed, privacy-safe NetworkProtocol audit with an explicit barrier against automatic remediation.
independent_technical_reasoning: NetworkProtocol aggregates service configuration such as enabled states and ports, which differs from Ethernet interface addressing. Its value depends on validating each protocol block and preserving unknown vendor fields rather than merely formatting JSON. The same payload can reveal the management attack surface, so exported endpoints require redaction. Most importantly, an unexpected disabled service or port is an observed mismatch, not authority to PATCH it; this row remains a pure read and can therefore be fully automated.
